artworks.title: The Pleiades
artworks.description: Vedder's Metropolitan Museum canvas gathers Atlas' seven star-daughters in a luminous void, each with a threaded star. Electra — the Samothracian Pleiad who bore Dardanus and Iasion to Zeus, and whose dimmed star was later read as the 'lost Pleiad' mourning Troy — stands among the celestial sisters, not the Mycenaean princess of the same name.

artworks.title: The Dance of the Pleiades (Star Lore of All Ages, plate)
artworks.description: Olcott's 1911 star-lore plate reproduces Vedder's circling Pleiades as dancers of the night sky. Electra is one of the seven — mother of the Trojan line through Dardanus — carried into popular astronomy as myth and constellation together.

artworks.title: Study for "The Pleiades"
artworks.description: Metropolitan Museum study for Vedder's Pleiades: the seven sisters take shape in chalk and wash — among them Electra, the Pleiad of Samothrace whose son Dardanus founded the line of Troy.

artworks.title: The Rising of the Pleiades (illustration to Hesiod)
artworks.description: Flaxman's outline for Hesiod's Works and Days: the rising of the Pleiades marks the farmer's calendar — the star-cluster that is also Electra and her sisters written into harvest time.

music.title: Atlàntida
music.description: Falla's unfinished scenic cantata after Verdaguer draws on the Atlantis myth and the Pleiades' oceanic memory — Electra's star-sisterhood as Iberian mythic backdrop.

popCulture.title: Electra (Pleiad)
popCulture.description: One of the seven Pleiades; by Zeus mother of Dardanus and Iasion — the star-nymph of Samothrace, not Agamemnon's daughter.
